newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Dutch KNP BT Q3 profit drops 67 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dutch KNP BT Q3 profit drops 67 pct.

text.p: Dutch paper, printing and office machinery group KNP BT posted sharply lower third-quarter profits on Thursday but repeated a forecast that the second half of 1996 would show an improvement on the first.

Third-quarter net profit from ordinary operations tumbled 67 percent to 38 million guilders ($22.4 million) from a previous 116 million, dragged down by a seven-million guilder operating loss at its majority-owned Austrian paper making unit.
In the third quarter of 1995, the KNP Leykam unit posted operating profits of 108 million guilders.
But KNP BT reiterated a forecast of higher second-half ordinary net profits from the first half's 101 million guilders.

"Given that the fourth quarter is seasonally the best for KNP BT, we maintain our earlier forecast that the net result over the second half of the year will be slightly higher than in the first half," the company said in a statement.
KNP BT shares opened down 0.30 cents at 37.70 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange after the results but recovered to trade unchanged at 38 guilders mid-morning.
Analysts said the figures held no surprises and were nearly on target.
They had expected the company to post a third-quarter net from ordinary operations of between 33 million and 45 million guilders, with the consensus at 39 million.
"Overall, the results were as expected," said Bank Labouchere's Ad van de Laar.
But he said KNP Leykam's results were better than he had forecast. "Paper prices are recovering a touch," he said.

However, KNP BT said the 72-percent owned paper division was still struggling with low margins. "The sales volumes were good (in the third quarter), but the margins remained at a very low level," it said.
KNP said in September it would seek a partner for the troubled division. ($ = 1.695 Dutch Guilders)
